title: PwC talent leader on the firm's new AI critical thinking certificate
excerpt: PwC announced a critical thinking certification to sharpen AI-era skills for 85,000 people. Its talent leader said feedback so far has been positive.
content_html:
2026-11-23T19:09:27.549Z

As Business Insider recently reported, PwC is rolling out a new certification program designed to ensure its employees sharpen the people skills that artificial intelligence can't replace.

The firm is releasing the Critical Thinking and Judgment certificate program in December to its more than 85,000 employees and partners in the US and Mexico, as well as across its Acceleration Centers, which support business operations.

The program includes online courses and hands-on practice, as employees will apply what they learn to their jobs, said Margaret Burke, firmwide talent acquisition and development leader for PwC US. Burke designed and developed the program alongside Yolanda Seals-Coffield, the chief people and inclusion officer at PwC US.

Burke said the certification comes after PwC recently identified 15 AI technical skills and 15 human skills — including adaptability and intellectual curiosity — that are essential for employees working in an AI-enabled workplace. As the company began reviewing its training curricula, critical thinking and judgment were two human skills from the list that stood out.

"We decided that every time we were teaching the AI skills, we had to be teaching the human skills that go alongside it," Burke said. "As technology becomes more embedded in everyday work, the ability to use AI effectively goes hand in hand with the human judgment needed to question, evaluate, and act on its outputs."

Burke said all employees and partners are expected to complete the virtual certification, which will take about five hours. After it launches internally, PwC will also make the program's framework available to universities to incorporate into their training next year.

Business Insider spoke with Burke about why this certification is necessary, what it involves, and how employees are responding.

The following has been edited for clarity and length.

Why is it important to train employees on critical thinking as AI becomes ubiquitous?

In the past, employees would have built judgment through their work by researching, analyzing, and learning from mistakes. But AI is taking on more of these day-to-day tasks and changing how we formulate our judgment and develop critical thinking, which is essential to our work.

We wanted something that would make our people stop and think about it. The certification program gives our people a framework for practicing and strengthening these skills when AI is involved.

The framework provides a consistent way for people to think about how they're working with AI — in terms of how to review, evaluate, and make decisions from AI outputs, as well as when inputting things into AI and working with an AI agent. What are the steps that I should take to make sure that the work is right?

How did PwC develop the program?

PwC developed the proprietary framework and methodology in-house. We also worked with professors and leading academic experts to help us shape, inform, and give evidence to the framework.

We began work on it in August and have been moving at pace to meet the moment. We believe there is no time to waste in preparing our people further, given the speed at which AI is transforming work.

What does the certification program involve?

It starts with an online critical thinking diagnostic. Employees answer questions to analyze how they think and how they reach judgments. They will then be categorized by thinking style, such as a questioner, analyst, visionary, connector, or pragmatist. Based on thinking style, the program will identify their strengths and areas where they need to focus more.

Then, they'll take online learning modules on the critical-thinking and judgment framework based on their specific role within the organization. This section focuses on how to interact with AI in their work — including clarifying what an AI-produced outcome should be, challenging that output, correcting any mistakes, and repeating the process as necessary, before communicating the AI's result.

The program also includes a series of masterclass videos featuring professors, internal experts, and people in the tech field discussing skills related to judgment.

What opportunities will employees have to practice these skills throughout the program?

The learning experience includes multiple opportunities for participants to practice applying the framework through personalized simulations relevant to their roles, supported by on-the-job tools and team-based exercises. This includes on-the-job practice between learning modules with feedback from their leaders. The program culminates in a final simulation as part of the certificate requirements.

An AI coach is available to everyone to help them reinforce and apply critical thinking and judgment skills to their everyday work. It's designed to provide ongoing, personalized support beyond the formal learning experience.

How have employees responded?

Positively. When it was announced, we said that people who wanted early access to the certification could sign up. We've already seen about 3,000 employees and partners sign up.

It's going to be expected that all of our people complete the certification. We will measure and track completions. It will be part of their performance metrics at the end of the year — not their score, just whether or not they completed the certification.

What impact do you hope the certification has on your employees and partners?

Our goal has always been to make critical thinking and sound judgment a consistent part of how our people work and make decisions. In the age of AI, we want to make sure they're even more focused, whether AI is involved or not. They may need to think differently or look for blind spots they may not have previously encountered. We want employees to confidently challenge assumptions, evaluate information, identify gaps, and make informed decisions.

We'll assess how these skills are applied through ongoing observation and performance feedback. Ultimately, success means they're better equipped to navigate complex situations, exercise independent judgment, and deliver high-quality work for clients.
